decision: Move toSingleLine + CONTROL_CHAR_RE into luca-tools and re-export from luca-cli handoff-transport.ts
alternatives: duplicate the escaper in the hook handler (forbidden); move it into luca-core (outside the scope fence); shell out to the built luca CLI (PATH-dependent
process startup on the SessionStart critical path)
reasoning: luca-tools cannot import luca-cli (dep graph is luca-cli -> luca-tools -> luca-core), the handler must reach the escaper, and re-exporting keeps every phase-2 import site byte-unchanged
risk: the re-export is an indirection a later refactor could undo, reintroducing a second definition

decision: MAX_INTENT_PREVIEW = 120 chars and MAX_LISTED = 5 entries; escape first, then hard-cap
alternatives: no intent preview at all (mirrors phase-2 list
but then the notice tells you nothing actionable); 256 to match toSingleLine's own cap; no entry-count cap
reasoning: the notice is read into context at turn zero, so an unbounded mailbox would dominate the session opening; 120 chars is enough to recognise a work order without carrying a payload, and capping after escaping keeps the bound true despite escape expansion
risk: 120 may truncate mid-word on genuinely useful intents, pushing users to luca handoff list --json more often than necessary

decision: The hook does not compute or surface the autoAcceptable annotation that luca handoff list --json carries
alternatives: mirror the list handler exactly and show (auto-acceptable)
which would require reading .luca/config.json handoff.autoAcceptFrom on the SessionStart critical path
reasoning: surfacing an auto-acceptable marker is an invitation for the agent to advance pending -> accepted unprompted, which is the one thing this phase must never do; it also removes a config read from the hot path
risk: an operator who relies on the annotation must run luca handoff list to see it

decision: Defer the transport-injection seam needed to test describeCompleteHopFailure hop-2 wiring; confirm the in-progress single-hop recovery coverage instead via ac-22
alternatives: add the seam to phase 2's luca-cli accept/complete handlers in this phase
reasoning: the seam lives in handlers this phase does not otherwise touch, and phase 4 (lu-handoff-send / lu-handoff-accept skills) exercises exactly those handlers, so it lands more cheaply there
risk: the hop-2 recovery sentence stays deletable with a green suite for one more phase

decision: Specify escaping positionally — every rendered string field except id and status — instead of enumerating a field list
alternatives: keep the enumerated list and just append origin.repoName to it
reasoning: round 1 proved the list form had already drifted in a single drafting pass: target.repoPath was escaped but never rendered while origin.repoName was rendered but never escaped; a list must be re-audited on every render change, the positional rule cannot desync
risk: a future field whose rendering genuinely must not be escaped needs an explicit documented exception rather than silent omission

decision: Probe all seven degradation entry paths separately (ac-13/14/15/23.x plus new ac-24/25/26) rather than letting D8 assert a blanket silent-degradation claim over three probes
alternatives: narrow D8's wording to the three modes actually probed and defer the rest
reasoning: D8 named five modes and probed three; the two gaps included the empty-homedir residual phase 2 filed and never closed, where mailboxDirFor returns a RELATIVE .luca/handoff that existsSync resolves against cwd — a repo-local directory silently read as the mailbox. An error banner at every session start in an unrelated repo is this phase's worst regression, so the claim must not outrun the evidence
risk: ac-26 uses chmod 0o000 to force a non-ok list result, which does not deny access when tests run as root

decision: Add ac-27 (bundled handler exists under dist/claude after bun run build) and ac-28 (luca-tools declares a test script), plus a required manual live-session observation in execute/summary.md
alternatives: stop verification at the compiled settings.json
reasoning: every criterion could be green while the hook never fires in any real repo: the bundling step and the harness invocation were both unverified, and luca-tools has no test script so its tests never run in the filtered suite
risk: ac-27 depends on bun run build succeeding, which is slower than the other checks; the live-session observation is human-supplied and cannot be automated

decision: Covered ac-25 empty-homedir via a pure extracted guard (resolve-mailbox-dir.ts) plus a decoy-reachability demo, instead of the planned HOME='' spawn
alternatives: inject a homedir seam into the handler for tests
reasoning: Verified empirically that POSIX os.homedir() falls back to the passwd DB when HOME is empty (HOME= bun -e printed the real home), so the planned spawn can never make the process observe an empty homedir. That case would have been green whether or not the guard existed - the exact trivially-passing shape the plan forbade. Extracting the guard makes it deterministically fix-sensitive.
risk: The guard is now proven at the unit level rather than through a live process, so a future refactor could drop the call site in handler.ts while the unit test stays green; anti-06 and the handler source assertions partially offset this.
reviewHint: Confirm handler.ts still calls resolveMailboxDir before mailboxDirFor - that call site is the guard

decision: Rebuilt CONTROL_CHAR_RE and the escape outputs from String.fromCharCode instead of copying the source-level escapes verbatim
alternatives: re-export from luca-core (blocked by the scope fence)
reasoning: The plan asked for a verbatim move, but writing the file with literal backslash-u escapes decoded them into RAW control characters on disk - the exact mangling the plan's integrity rule #4 warns about, and it silently broke grep on the file. Char-code construction is escape-free ASCII that survives any pipeline. Behavior was proven identical to the original across all 200 code points plus the 600-char truncation case before the original was deleted.
risk: The regex source string now differs textually from the old one, so any probe comparing regex .source rather than behavior would see a difference; no such probe exists.
reviewHint: Escaper behavior parity was proven by differential test over code points 0-199, not by textual diff

decision: Kept BOTH MF-1 halves: escape angle brackets in the shared escaper AND add a per-invocation randomUUID nonce to the containment delimiter
alternatives: nonce only (leaves the sender able to write brackets into the human-facing list view)
reasoning: The audit's lesson is that the delimiter is part of the attacker's alphabet; escaping removes the alphabet and the nonce removes predictability, so a future rendered field added without toSingleLine still cannot forge the boundary
risk: renderInboxNotice is no longer deterministic by default; mitigated by an injectable nonce parameter used by every test
reviewHint: Confirm the nonce parameter is test-only and that no production caller passes one

decision: MF-4: made BOTH resolve-mailbox-dir.ts and the luca-core transport dynamic imports inside main, rather than adding a process.on('uncaughtException') handler
alternatives: dynamic import of the transport only
reasoning: resolve-mailbox-dir.ts statically imports mailboxDirFor from the same luca-core module, so deferring only the transport would have left the graph in the module-eval phase and the fix would have read as done while doing nothing; render-inbox-notice.ts stays static because its luca-core import is type-only and erased
risk: A future contributor re-adding a static luca-core import silently reopens the hole; guarded by the p3-mf-4 check and the handler.test.ts static-import assertion
reviewHint: Verify no static import line in handler.ts mentions luca-core or resolve-mailbox-dir
